segments.name: Alaska Airlines
segments.description: Scheduled passenger and cargo air transportation on Alaska's Boeing aircraft throughout North America, Latin America, Asia, and the Pacific.
segments.evidence: Alaska Airlines - includes scheduled air transportation on Alaska's Boeing aircraft for passengers and cargo.

segments.name: Hawaiian Airlines
segments.description: Scheduled passenger and cargo air transportation on Hawaiian's Boeing and Airbus aircraft, serving guests traveling to, from, or within the Hawaiian Islands.
segments.evidence: Hawaiian Airlines - includes scheduled air transportation on Hawaiian's Boeing and Airbus aircraft for passengers and cargo.

segments.name: Regional
segments.evidence: Regional - includes Horizon's and other third-party carriers' scheduled air transportation on E175 aircraft for passengers under CPAs.

revenueModel.text: The company earns most of its revenue from passengers buying tickets, plus loyalty program revenue from co-branded credit cards and partners, and cargo and other revenue from freight, mail, and services.
revenueModel.evidence: The majority of our revenue is generated by transporting passengers.

changes.text: In 2024, Air Group acquired Hawaiian Holdings, adding Hawaiian Airlines as a reportable segment.
changes.evidence: Hawaiian Holdings, Inc. was acquired by Air Group in 2024.

changes.text: In 2025, Alaska Airlines' and Hawaiian Airlines' operations were combined under a single FAA operating certificate, though both remain reportable segments.
changes.evidence: On that date, Alaska Airlines' and Hawaiian Airlines' operations were combined under Alaska's Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) operating certificate.

changes.text: In 2026, the company will report a single reportable segment for Passenger Air Transportation.
changes.evidence: In 2026, the company's segments disclosure will change to reflect a single reportable segment for Passenger Air Transportation, which includes revenue and expenses associated with the transportation of passengers on Boeing, Airbus, and E175 aircraft.
